newsitem.title: FRANCE: French film star Beatrice Dalle guilty of drug use.
newsitem.headline: French film star Beatrice Dalle guilty of drug use.

text.p: Sultry French film actress Beatrice Dalle was convicted of illegal drugs use on Thursday, but the court agreed not to register the conviction on her record so she could continue to pursue her career in the United States.

Recording the conviction would have prevented her from obtaining the U.S. visas she needs to go on filming "The Blackout," now in production in Florida with independent U.S. director Abel Ferrara and co-stars Matthew Modine and model Claudia Schiffer.
Dalle, 32-year-old star of the international hit "Betty Blue", was fined 20,000 francs ($4,000) but the court dropped a more serious charge of drugs trafficking.
Dalle had been placed under investigation in August 1995 after half a gram of heroin and half a gram of cocaine were found by police at her home.
Dalle denied the charge and said the drugs had been left by friends who had borrowed her flat. She later acknowledged she had completed a drugs treatment programme.

The pouting actress, often cast in the role of an unstable femme fatale, was convicted in 1992 of stealing jewels from a Paris boutique. She received at that time a six-month suspended jail term and a 20,000 franc fine.
